checksums.name: none_found
checksums.formula_detail: No checksum/CRC computation over save payload bytes was found in any traced function. The only 'verify' primitive (0x08032edc) is a write-then-read-back equality check against the data the caller just supplied, not a stored/derived integrity value. Brute-force sum8/xor8/complement tests against the trailer-looking bytes (0xD8, 0x41, 0x5A, 0x73) at every 8-byte-aligned prefix range did not produce a code-corroborated match.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3 transfer primitive (DmaXfer): programs src/dst/control for DMA3, sets enable bit 0x80000000, busy-waits on control-word bit 15. Shared by both EEPROM read and write bitstream paths.
EepromReadSector(sector, dst[4xu16]). Builds a 2-bit read opcode + 6-bit sector-address bitstream, DMAs it out to 0xD000000, DMAs 0x44 (68) response bits back in, unpacks 4x16-bit words.

EepromWriteSector(sector, src[4xu16]). Builds a 2-bit write opcode + 6-bit sector address + 64 data bits, DMAs it to 0xD000000 with length param+0x43, brackets the hardware busy-poll with 0x08032c04/0x08032c8c.

EepromReadVerify(sector, expected[4xu16]) = calls EepromReadSector then compares word-by-word against expected; returns 0 on match, 0x8000 on mismatch. Write-confirmation only, not a payload checksum.
Small wrapper around the EEPROM write busy-poll; sets/clears an internal flag pair, no data transformation observed.
Paired wrapper with 0x08032c04, clears the flag set by it on completion.
ReadEepromBlock(startSector, buf, len). Loops 8 bytes at a time calling EepromReadSector directly into buf then EepromReadVerify; handles non-multiple-of-8 tails via an 8-byte scratch buffer.
WriteEepromBlock(startSector, buf, len). Loops 8 bytes at a time calling EepromWriteSector then EepromReadVerify; handles tails via read-modify-write of an 8-byte scratch buffer.
Acquire-style wrapper called before every traced block read/write pair; sets a busy/lock flag. Exact mechanism (reentrancy guard vs interrupt mask) unresolved.
Release-style wrapper paired with 0x0800deb8; clears the busy/lock flag.

open_questions: Does any checksum/CRC protect save payload bytes anywhere in the (currently unresolved) jump-table targets not covered by this decompilation? No evidence of one was found in the 292 traced functions.

What writes real gameplay data into a slot body (score, level, items, etc.)? No caller of the EEPROM write path other than the boot-time auto-formatter (0x08022680, called only from 0x080281d8) was found in this workspace -- the in-game 'Save' action's caller chain is unmapped.
What is the true meaning of the per-slot stepped-by-4 byte at relative body offset +0x08 (observed 0x00/0x04/0x08 across slots 0/1/2)? No reader was traced.

Is the apparent 'stack garbage' region (relative body offset +0x28 through +0x9F) ever actually read by any game code, or is it truly dead? No reader was found, but absence of a traced reader in a partial decompilation is not proof of absence.

What are the concrete absolute RAM addresses for the save struct mirrors? All relevant pointers in the decompiled code are unresolved Ghidra globals (_DAT_*), so 'RAM Mirror Addr' is UNKNOWN for every field.
Both available .sav samples represent pre-gameplay/blank-init states; no sample of a real played save exists in this workspace to validate any body-field hypothesis against actual game state changes.
